prediction: #433, NBA Live 07. Flag off (A) reproduces surfdl1008's 1-1791525340 baseline: `reuse` 10.70 ms/flip (fin 0.5/flip) and `surfupd` 8.74 ms/flip (fence 0.5/flip) on alternating flips, all callers 19.33 ms/flip median, ph_Fin 13.8, ph_GPU 21.3, ph_Tot 36.6, gfps 22.17. Flag on (B): the reuse rebind detaches (reuse <= 1.0 ms/flip, detach >= 0.4 per flip), and a flip batch that carries no display surface is marked pending at the flip (nodisp >= 0.3 per flip) so the surfupd rebind that follows leaves it pending, as #474 does for the display pre-download, instead of waiting its fence; a rebinding upload that reads the batch's bytes still waits (counted `pre`), so the ceiling also tests that NBA 07's surfupd uploads mostly do not overlap the flip batch (surfupd <= 2.0 ms/flip); the sum of all [sdcall] waits per flip at most half of A's; ph_Fin down at least 6.0 ms/frame; gfps up at least 2.0 (ph_GPU 21.3 stays, so the ceiling is the GPU, not 30). Pixels unchanged, as for NBA 2005.

legs.V (validity): V1: B's logcat carries '[surfgpu] on' (the env reached the process). V2: A's does not. V3: both arms have >= 5 post-mark [sdcall] windows. V4: no thermal pause in either arm (decompose.py's THERMAL line). A V failure voids the pair: it goes to identification (what failed and why), never a blind rerun.
legs.P0 (the wait is there to remove): A, flag off, reproduces the baseline wait this fix targets: the named caller's median ms per flip post-mark is at least the registered floor. A P0 failure means the scene did not reach the measured state; the pair is not scored on P1-P4.
legs.P1 (the caller drops): B's `reuse` wait (and, where registered, `surfupd`) per flip is at most the registered ceiling, and the switch acted: [surfgpu] detach= (and nodisp=) per flip at least the registered floor. If reuse drops but detach does not, the drop is not this switch's.
legs.P2 (the wait did not move): The SUM of every [sdcall] caller's wait per flip (median of windows), B over A, is at most the registered ratio. A wait that moved from reuse to surfupd, rotation `pre` or a new caller is counted here, which is the async794 failure mode.
legs.P3 (ph_Fin): decompose.py's all-row ph_Fin, A minus B, is at least the registered drop in ms per frame.
legs.P4 (gfps): decompose.py's all-row gfps (mark-restricted), B minus A, is at least the registered gain. Read only after the hold frames show a game in play with players moving in both arms.
legs.M (moving player, hand-read): The hold frames of both arms, minutes apart, show live gameplay (score/clock advancing, players in different positions), not a menu, replay or paused state. If either arm's hold frames do not, its fps is not read.
legs.X (pixels, hand-read): sg_judge.py --floor prints route-frame regions (gpunonrender/regioncheck.py: 4x4 grid, tol 8, FPS overlay masked) for B vs A and for A vs the older flag-off run on the same route. PASS: B vs A differs in no more regions than the floor's 2x, and every differing region is an animated panel (crowd, scoreboard, clock) on inspection; any region showing missing, stale or garbled surface content (a black/old court, wrong depth occlusion, a stale HUD) is a correctness FAIL regardless of count. The disc leg is surfgpu1009-golden.json.
legs.R (reported, not scored): B's residual: record ms per flip, spl= up/dl/cmpl per flip (cmpl > 0 means the splice could not cover and completed on the CPU at SDC_SURF_UPDATE), defer_full, shader_cache of both arms (B runs first on a new apk and starts cold, so B's cold-cache compiles bias AGAINST this prediction).

expect_note: Named rules, not capture keys: a soak writes no captures. sg_judge.py scores each key against these thresholds and fails any key it has no reader for.
